name: JST PH 2-pin power inlet
//: The thing nobody lists among their modules, which is why generated boards kept coming out with a power rail that had exactly one member. A module list is a list of CONSUMERS; something still has to bring the supply onto the board, and physically that something is a connector. It is in the library so it can be named in a requirements file like any other part, rather than hand-added to the generated design afterwards.
//rail: This inlet is declared to supply the MOTOR rail because that is the rail a module list cannot source for itself — logic and ground come from the microcontroller module. An inlet for a different rail is a different file, not a flag: which rail arrives on a connector is a fact about the harness, and a part that could be silently repointed at any rail would wire a 6 V pack to 3.3 V logic without anything noticing.

power.note: From the external pack. NOT regulated by this board and NOT referenced to anything until GND below is joined — the two domains share ground and nothing else.
The single point where the motor supply's return meets board ground. If the harness also grounds elsewhere, that is a ground loop through the motor return.

pin_order_proof.source: Pad 1 is VCC: this record's own convention for a generic 2-pin inlet, not read from a document.

body_mm.source: JST PH series drawing, B2B-PH-K-S: 7.9 mm across the 2-pin housing, 5.8 mm deep including the latch

host_requirements: Size the inlet for the STALL current, not the running current. A lid motor stalls every time something blocks it, and JST PH is rated 2 A per contact.
This connector and any other 2-pin connector on the board can be cross-plugged unless one of them is keyed or a different series. Swapping a motor supply into an audio output destroys the amplifier.
Fuse or current-limit upstream. Nothing on the board protects this rail.

Check the CRIMP order of a hand-made harness before first power: JST PH housings are keyed, so the mate cannot be reversed, but the crimps can — and 6 V into a motor driver's ground is not recoverable. Mark pin 1 on the silkscreen.

contact_rating_a.source: JST PH series datasheet, current rating per contact at 20 C rise

simulation.skip: a connector is wiring, not a part to simulate; the simulator powers the board itself
